exposure: measurement of the angle of progression by sonography
control group (angle of progression not communicated)
study group (angle of progression communicated to obstetrician)
outcome: maternal complications (third and fourth-degree perineal tears, failed vaginal instrumental delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, hysterectomy)
neonatal outcomes (Apgar score <5 at 10 minutes, umbilical arterial pH <7.10, neonatal wounds, neonatal intensive care unit admission)
cohort: 45 women at term with a singleton cephalic fetus in a clinical occiput anterior position after a prolonged 2-hour second stage of labor with uncertain fetal head engagement
finding: Measuring the angle of progression by sonography in addition to digital examination in cases of uncertain fetal head engagement showed promising results in decreasing cesarean delivery rates, though further research is needed.
mod_finding: Measuring the angle of progression during labor in cases of uncertain fetal head engagement showed promise in reducing cesarean delivery rates.
